candidates.name: Typhlitis
support_spans: recurrent right abdomen pain progressing to involve the entire abdomen
edematous thickening of the intestinal wall in the ascending colon with peripheral exudative changes
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging results are consistent with typhlitis, which is an inflammation of the cecum.

candidates.name: Neutropenic colitis
support_spans: leukocytopenia
neutrophil percentage: 85.40%
candidates.why: The patient's history of leukocytopenia and current neutrophil percentage are consistent with neutropenic colitis.

candidates.name: Pseudomembranous colitis
support_spans: edema in all layers of intestinal wall
diffuse infiltration of neutrophils with presence of abscesses
candidates.why: The patient's histological examination results are consistent with pseudomembranous colitis, which is caused by an overgrowth of Clostridioides difficile.

candidates.name: Bacterial peritonitis
support_spans: Ascites culture yielded growth of Escherichia coli
small quantity of ascites
candidates.why: The patient's ascites culture results and presence of ascites are consistent with bacterial peritonitis.
